name: USDT
label: legit
why: Tether USD, the largest stablecoin, traded on every major exchange since 2017. Its owner (a multisig contract) can mint, blacklist, pause and set fees: TetherToken.sol lines 250-425 are onlyOwner. A legitimate token can hold dangerous powers, which is why powers alone are not a verdict.

name: USDC
label: legit
why: Circle's USD Coin. An upgradeable proxy (FiatTokenV2_2) whose owner, a wallet, can replace the master minter, blacklister and pauser (FiatTokenV1.sol:380, Blacklistable.sol:89, Pausable.sol:87, all onlyOwner); minting, blacklisting and pausing themselves belong to those roles.

name: DAI
label: legit
why: MakerDAO's Dai stablecoin. No owner: minting is gated by `wards` (governance contracts), so neither the deployer nor anyone else can mint. Deployed through MakerDAO's deployment contracts.

name: PEPE
label: legit
why: The largest memecoin by market value, on major exchanges since 2023. Ownership renounced (owner() is the zero address), so its blacklist function can no longer be used.

name: UNI
label: legit
why: Uniswap's governance token. No owner; minting belongs to the minter (the governance timelock) and is rate-limited, so neither the deployer nor a stranger can mint.

name: LINK
label: legit
why: Chainlink's token, live since 2017 and on every major exchange. A plain ERC-677 token without owner functions.

name: SHIB
label: legit
why: Shiba Inu, on major exchanges since 2021. A plain ERC-20 without owner functions.

name: BRETT
label: legit
why: Base's largest memecoin, listed on major exchanges since 2024. Ownership renounced, so its fee and limit setters are dead.

name: AERO
label: legit
why: Aerodrome's token, the main DEX on Base since 2023. No owner; minting belongs to Aerodrome's Minter contract (setMinter/mint check msg.sender == minter).

name: DEGEN
label: legit
why: Degen, the Farcaster community token, on major exchanges since 2024. Its owner (a contract) can pause transfers (DegenToken.sol:127, onlyOwner); mint is onlyOwner too but locked until mintingAllowedAfter = 1830297600 (2028-01-01).

name: ASN
label: scam
why: Honeypot. In the pair's first 40,000 blocks, 24 wallets paid 7.93 WETH in; the only wallet that ever sold was the deployer (0.56 WETH). sellTax() is 100 and the owner can change it: on an Anvil fork, setSellTax(1) from the owner moved it to 1 and the same call from another account reverted.

name: QTC
label: scam
why: Honeypot. 28 wallets paid 30.64 WETH into the pair; one wallet sold (7.07 WETH). The verified source emits fake Transfer events to hide the minting account (QTC.sol _mint sets `adr` and logs the mint as coming from `holder`). The deployer holds all the LP tokens.

name: GTA6
label: scam
why: Honeypot behind a clean front: ownership renounced and LP burned, yet 31 wallets bought (0.85 WETH) and only one ever sold, for nothing. The trap sits in the MAxTradingIdentifierLimits modifier on _transfer.

name: FREEDOM250
label: scam
why: Honeypot behind a clean front: ownership renounced and LP burned, yet of 35 buying wallets 33 never sold (2.22 WETH paid in) while two insiders took 3.24 WETH out.

name: AMERICA250
label: scam
why: Honeypot. Of 37 buying wallets, 36 never sold (2.41 WETH paid in); the only seller took 3.43 WETH out. Ownership renounced, but the deployer still holds all the LP tokens. Launched three thousand blocks after FREEDOM250, same theme.

name: DREAM
label: scam
why: Honeypot, then rug. 36 of 37 buying wallets never sold (2.80 WETH paid in); about 13 hours after launch the deployer removed the liquidity (Burn in tx 0xf2a78472…, block 25456097, sent by the deployer). What is left in the pair is the 1000-wei minimum and Uniswap's protocol-fee LP.

name: ARC
label: scam
why: Rug pull. 12 wallets paid 12.98 WETH for it; four days after launch (block 26005261) the deployer removed the liquidity, leaving only the 1000-wei minimum and Uniswap's protocol-fee LP in the pair.

name: EWL
label: scam
why: Rug pull. 51 wallets bought (0.41 WETH in all) and the deployer removed the liquidity 4.7 hours after launch (block 25977782).

name: Indy
label: scam
why: Honeypot. 41 wallets bought (1.79 WETH) and none of them ever sold; the only seller was the deployer, who took 2.29 WETH out and still holds all the LP tokens. Ownership renounced.

name: USA
label: scam
why: Honeypot, then rug. 22 of 23 buying wallets never sold (0.76 WETH paid in); 60 blocks after launch the deployer, who is also the owner, removed the liquidity (Burn in tx 0xd64b0615…, block 25457760).
